parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the focal length of a converging lens by two methods. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Figs. 4.1 and 4.2. Fig. 4.1

ms.label: 4(a)
ms.text: both f values present, clearly in cm

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Arrange the illuminated object, lens and mirror as shown in Fig. 4.1. Set the distance D between the mirror and the illuminated object to 20 cm.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Move the lens until a sharp image appears on the front of the card C by the side of the illuminated object.

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Measure, and record in Table 4.1, the distance f between the lens and the illuminated object. f is a value for the focal length of the lens in this experiment. Table 4.1 D / cm f / cm 20 40 [1]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) Repeat steps (a)(i) to (a)(iii) for a distance D = 40 cm.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Use your results from the table to calculate F 1 , an average value for f . F 1 = ...........................................................[1]

ms.label: 4(c)
ms.text:
both v values present
correct calculations of f
both to at least 1 d.p.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Set up the lens, illuminated object and screen as shown in Fig. 4.2. Fig. 4.2

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Set the distance u between the illuminated object and the lens to 20.0 cm.

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Move the screen until a sharp image of the illuminated object appears on the screen.

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Measure, and record in Table 4.2, the distance v between the lens and the screen. Table 4.2 u / cm v / cm f / cm 20.0 30.0 [3]

parts.label: v
parts.text: (v) Repeat steps (c)(ii) to (c)(iv) for a value of u = 30.0 cm.

parts.label: vi
parts.text: (vi) For each value of u , calculate and record in the table the focal length f , using your results from the table and the equation f = uv ( u + v ) .
